subject.title: Feature Request: Gateway lifecycle hooks (onSubagentComplete, onToolCallThreshold, onTurnComplete)

question: Should OpenClaw expose subagent completion, turn completion, and tool-call threshold behavior to workspace/internal hooks, keep them in typed plugin hooks, or split observation-only and mutating semantics between the two surfaces?
rationale: The missing source surface is clear, but the permanent payload, authority, ordering, threshold configuration, and security boundary are public API/product decisions that automation should not lock in.

options.title: Stage observation-only internal hooks
options.body: Add safe, non-mutating internal events for subagent and turn completion while leaving mutation, blocking, and sensitive child/session access in typed plugin hooks.

options.title: Keep lifecycle hooks plugin-only
options.body: Treat typed plugin hooks as the supported lifecycle surface and narrow this issue away from HOOK.md workspace hooks that need sensitive runtime state.

options.title: Design one lifecycle model first
options.body: Pause implementation until maintainers define a combined internal/plugin lifecycle model covering payloads, ordering, thresholds, and security limits.

recommendation.title: Stage observation-only internal hooks
recommendation.body: Add safe, non-mutating internal events for subagent and turn completion while leaving mutation, blocking, and sensitive child/session access in typed plugin hooks.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice centers on typed hook contracts and lifecycle/security boundaries where recent related history points most strongly.
